source.title: FlatMatch: Bridging Labeled Data and Unlabeled Data with Cross-Sharpness for Semi-Supervised Learning
source.authors: Zhuo Huang; Li Shen; Jun Yu; Bo Han; Tong-Liang Liu

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the extracted results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper directly measures the labeled/unlabeled loss and generalization mismatch in semi-supervised training and reports that its proposed method reduces the loss gap. Its experiments are about SSL generalization and flatness, not the listed versions about memorization, architecture comparisons, optimizers, batches, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test errors for SSL methods, sharpness measurements, gradient norms, and labeled/unlabeled loss comparisons. Most benchmark error rates compare the authors’ proposed method with other SSL methods; those do not measure any listed claim version. Rows below cover the explicit labeled/unlabeled loss-gap finding and the reported sharpness comparison relevant to the claim’s generalization-measure subject. Figure-only values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: FlatMatch uses the premise that flatter solutions generalize better to design an SSL regularizer, but its results test none of V1–V8. Its sharpness measure uses an absolute ℓ2 perturbation bound on validation loss, without magnitude scaling, train/test-gap rankings, or comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures required by V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that cross-sharpness regularization bridges labeled and unlabeled learning and improves SSL test performance in many settings. They also acknowledge limitations with extremely scarce labels and propose fixed pseudo-labels to stabilize sharpness computation; FlatMatch-e reduces computational cost with some performance loss.
record.recipe_differences: Semi-supervised image classification training with cross-sharpness and unlabeled data; the listed claim versions concern supervised generalization, architecture, optimizer, batch size, dropout, sharpness-gap correlations, and memorized-example removal.
record.method_sensitivity: The labeled-data count affects performance and the stability of sharpness computation; perturbation magnitude ρ affects test performance, with degradation reported above 0.25; number of fixed pseudo-labeled examples also affects performance. FlatMatch’s loss difference between labeled and unlabeled data is reported as significantly smaller than FixMatch’s.

fits_no_version.finding: Labeled loss approaches zero faster than unlabeled loss in FixMatch and FlatMatch; FlatMatch has a smaller labeled/unlabeled loss difference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-sharpness regularization can reduce the mismatch between labeled and unlabeled training losses in SSL.

fits_no_version.finding: FlatMatch has the lowest reported validation-loss sharpness curves among the compared methods on CIFAR10 and SVHN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-sharpness training can reduce validation-loss sensitivity to absolute ℓ2-bounded parameter perturbations.

record.problems: The paper’s labeled/unlabeled loss-gap comparison is reported for a single setting and is not the train/test generalization gap in the claim. Sharpness results are qualitative in the supplied text and do not establish a correlation with generalization gaps. The principal benchmark tables report mean ± values, but those SSL performance comparisons do not test the listed versions.
record.rows_left_out: The benchmark test-error tables (main Table 1; supplementary Tables 5–7), CIFAR100 ablations (Table 2), parameter sensitivity (Figure 5), gradient stability (Figure 6), and training efficiency (Figure 7) evaluate SSL method performance, sensitivity, or cost, rather than any listed claim version. Figure 8 sharpness values are not numerically recoverable from text and are not paired with train/test gaps; only the stated qualitative comparison is retained.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label held-out generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware training sharpness versus train/test gaps among similarly fitted networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T5 classification contradicts its correctly unlinked rows. Neither improved SSL test error nor reduced validation sharpness establishes the specific correlational claim in V7. No verdict labels are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error across widths beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.
Large-batch generalization gaps under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measured against train/test gaps within a convolutional family.
Test accuracy after removing memorized examples.

rows.subject: FixMatch
rows.operation_detail: Compared labeled and unlabeled loss values during training and their difference.
rows.measure: Loss difference between unlabeled and labeled data; the paper states FlatMatch’s loss difference is significantly smaller than FixMatch’s.
rows.value: FlatMatch loss difference is significantly smaller; numeric values not stated in text.
rows.locator: Supplementary Section D, Figure 11 and accompanying text; Figure 12
rows.note: The text says the labeled-data loss quickly converges to zero and is significantly smaller than unlabeled-data loss for both methods. This measures an SSL labeled/unlabeled loss mismatch, not a natural-label train/test generalization gap.
rows.check: The labeled/unlabeled training-loss difference does not measure any listed version. The reported reduction concerns FlatMatch relative to FixMatch, so the subject should be FlatMatch with FixMatch as baseline. Figure 11 describes trajectories during training; the last-checkpoint and 250-labels-per-class conditions are explicitly specified for Figure 12 and should not automatically be assigned to Figure 11.

rows.subject: FlatMatch
rows.operation_detail: Measured loss sharpness on a validation set as loss increase within an ℓ2-bounded parameter neighborhood.
rows.measure: Sharpness curve; authors report it is lowest among compared methods.
rows.baseline: FixMatch, Dash, and FreeMatch; fully supervised learning also shown as baseline.
rows.value: Lowest sharpness curve during training on CIFAR10; numeric values not stated in text.
rows.locator: Supplementary Section C, Figure 8 and accompanying text
rows.note: This is a sharpness comparison, but the text does not compare the measure with training/test gaps across networks; it therefore does not test V7.
rows.check: The qualitative lowest-sharpness finding is supported, but validation-loss sharpness under an absolute ℓ2 bound cannot establish V7. This is a comparison of the authors' method with SSL baselines, not a result row testing a listed version.
